title: ExtraWork: change-order capture for small subcontractors
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: Foremen record extra work by voice note or photo; AI turns it into a priced change order that the client's site manager signs on their phone before anyone forgets.
hook: "The site manager said 'just do it'. Three months later the main contractor called it original scope and refused to pay."
story:
**Mikael owns a 20-person electrical subcontracting firm in the UK.** On a typical job the main contractor's site manager asks his foreman to move six sockets and add a cable run. It is agreed by voice or on WhatsApp. The foreman means to write it down, but by Friday nobody remembers the hours or materials.

When Mikael invoices at the end of the project, the main contractor disputes the extras: there is **no signed paper**. He either writes the money off or accepts a big discount. Industry surveys say this is normal: **66% of subcontractors wrote off change-order revenue in the last year**. With ExtraWork, the foreman speaks a 20-second voice note, AI prices it from the rate card, and the site manager signs a link on his phone **the same day**.
whyNow: A 2026 Clearstory and Dodge Construction Network report says 92% of subcontractors are not always paid in full for change orders and 66% wrote off change-order revenue in the last 12 months. Cheap speech-to-text and LLMs make a voice-first tool possible for small firms for the first time. There is no regulatory deadline.
evidence: 92% of subcontractors are not always paid in full for change orders; only 6% say all are paid in full (vendor survey) [Clearstory]
66% of subcontractors wrote off change-order revenue in the last 12 months; change orders are discounted by an average of 22% (vendor survey) [Clearstory]
"Up to 36% of T&M tags never make it from the field to the office" (vendor claim) [Clearstory blog]
An older 2023 vendor survey estimated 32% of project revenue lost to unbilled or unpaid change orders (probably inflated) [Procore]
Procore starts at roughly $4.5k–10k a year with a one-year minimum; Fieldwire is free for 5 users, then $39/$64/$89 per user per month [Projul / BuilderSoftwareGuide]

whyReal.title: The money loss is direct
whyReal.text: Unpaid extras come straight out of profit. Even a 2–5% leak for a subcontractor with €2M revenue would be €40–100k a year (an inference, not a measured number), many times the price of the tool.

whyReal.title: The paper trail breaks in the field
whyReal.text: Extras are agreed verbally or on WhatsApp, and Clearstory says up to 36% of T&M tags never reach the office. General contractors then reclassify undocumented extras as original scope (eSUB).

whyReal.title: Existing tools are too big
whyReal.text: Clearstory serves enterprise contractors; Procore costs thousands a year with a one-year minimum. Small subcontractors need something as simple as WhatsApp.

whyReal.title: Same calls as SubDocs
whyReal.text: Jonatan can ask about subcontractor documents and unpaid extra work in one phone call to the same firms.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Specialist subcontractors with 5–50 staff: electrical, HVAC, drywall, painting, steel, scaffolding.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The owner or project manager. The daily users are the foremen.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK and Sweden (Jonatan's calls), then US and Australia, where the pain is higher than in Nordic markets with strong standard contracts.

solution.title: Foreman records the extra
solution.text: a voice note or typed line plus photos in a phone web app: "moved 6 sockets per site manager, 2 men 4 hours + materials".

solution.title: AI structures it
solution.text: speech-to-text + LLM pull out labour hours, materials and the reason for the extra work.

solution.title: Priced from the rate card
solution.text: the company's own rates turn the tag into a priced change order.

solution.title: Client signs on the phone
solution.text: the site manager gets a signing link; the signature is stored with timestamp, location and a PDF.

solution.title: Status board and reminders
solution.text: draft, sent, signed, invoiced, disputed; unsigned tags trigger reminder emails.

solution.title: Monthly export
solution.text: a CSV for invoicing so nothing signed is forgotten.

must: Progressive web app with voice-to-text and photo capture
AI extraction of labour hours, materials and reason
Company rate card that prices each tag
Client signing link with timestamp, location and PDF
Status board: draft, sent, signed, invoiced, disputed
later: Dispute pack: all tags and photos for a project in one PDF

techStack: E-signature via own signing page + PDF generation

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Post in r/Construction, r/electricians and on LinkedIn; Jonatan calls 15 Swedish and UK subcontractors (same calls as SubDocs). Give them a free "digital T&M tag" made with Typeform and a PDF template, and check whether foremen use it on real jobs within a week. Ask 5 firms for a €39/month pre-order.
Victor builds the phone app with voice and photo capture, AI extraction and the rate card.
Signing link, status board, reminders, CSV export and Stripe billing.
Pilot firms use it on live jobs; measure how many tags get signed and invoiced.

costs.note: Small EU cloud server or Vercel/Supabase free tiers + transactional email (report estimate)

Carrd / Typeform / Google Forms for the no-code test

risks.risk: The client's site manager may refuse to sign
risks.answer: Ask this in every interview; the signed link is optional, and a timestamped, photo-backed record still helps in disputes.
Voice-first, no login, under 30 seconds per tag; test real usage with the Typeform version first.
Strong standard contracts (AB04/ABT06) reduce disputes; push UK, US and Australia harder.

questions: Roughly how much extra work did you do last year that you were never paid for?
How does a foreman record extra work today, and how does it reach the office?
How often does the main contractor dispute a variation, and on what grounds?
How long is it from doing the extra work to invoicing it?
Would your clients' site managers sign on a phone link? Why or why not?
